steps.path: The briefcase icon under "Built in" in the pages rail on the left
steps.headline: Open or make a document, type something, close its tab — does your change stay in the file?
steps.changed: A separate test copy of YouCoded with the real Office editor. Office saves as you type, so use New document, or pick a COPY of one of your files, never an original.
steps.notice: Close the tab, then open the same file in Word or LibreOffice: your change is there. Reopen it in Office: it's there too, and the strip above the page said Saved.
steps.risk: It's a second window on your desktop; close it when you're done. Your own YouCoded isn't touched.

steps.path: An open document → Versions (top right of the Office page)
steps.headline: In the same test window, open Versions and restore the earliest one — does the document go back to how it was?
steps.changed: The same test window. Office keeps a copy when you open a file and every 10 minutes while you edit, and one more just before any restore.
steps.notice: After Restore the document reloads showing the older text, and Versions now also lists the copy it kept just before restoring.
steps.risk: Restore replaces the file with the older copy. Use the same copy or new file as before.

steps.path: Any open document; the test window already uses your current theme
steps.headline: Does the editor look like part of YouCoded in your theme — colours, corner roundness and menu font?
steps.changed: The same test window. Its menus, panels, buttons and rounding follow your theme, and it uses your theme's font.
steps.notice: Known and planned for later: document text shows in a plain serif font, and bullet points show as small dots, until the extra fonts are added.
steps.risk: Don't change the theme in the test window: it shares that setting with your own YouCoded, so your own app would change too.
